body:
**{metæffekt} Universe**
canonical name: [Pretix License Exception](https://github.com/org-metaeffekt/metaeffekt-universe/blob/main/src/main/resources/ae-universe/[p]/README.md#user-content-Pretix-License-Exception:~:text=Pretix%20License%20Exception)
short name: Pretix-License-Exception
category: Pretix License Exception
OSI status: _none_

**Comment**
No recommendation. I'm having a hard time to understand this exception. It appears to me like an oxymoron: "you must not follow remote network interaction when you do not expose it as a remote service." 
I'd rather chose the AGPL without exception. 

Looking forward to discuss this exception.

This is a weird one. I tend to agree with @karsten-klein. I'm having trouble parsing the intent of the exception, but the best I can understand it, I wouldn't consider it an "exception" as we think about them for [SPDX Exceptions List](https://spdx.org/licenses/exceptions-index.html) purposes.

The language at the top of the SPDX Exceptions List describes it as including those that _"grant an exception to a license condition or additional permissions beyond those granted in a license."_ Generally, that should not include anything that imposes an additional _restriction_ on rights that are otherwise granted in the underlying license.

Here, I agree with @karsten-klein that I can't understand how section 1 actually functions as an 'exception' or 'additional permission' as compared to AGPL-3.0 § 13.

Additionally, I am not convinced that section 2 is within the permitted scope of AGPL-3.0 § 7(b). My understanding is that AGPL § 7(b) is about requiring preservation of particular notices _on the licensed software itself_. By contrast, this section 2 language says that you must maintain the attribution notices _"at the bottom of all generated web pages."_ I'm not immediately recalling a good example, but my understanding has been that imposing the maintenance of notices like this _on generated output_ is generally outside the scope of permitted (A)GPL boundaries, other than situations where e.g. it is referring to particular copyrighted content that is inserted into the generated output. And even then, requiring the notice to be maintained "_at the bottom_" of the webpage goes too far in my view. That's a long-winded way of saying that this reads to me as an additional _restriction_.

Given all of that, I'm not in favor of adding this to the Exceptions List. This could still be represented in an SPDX license expression with a custom `AdditionRef-` form, as described in the thread at https://lists.spdx.org/g/spdx/topic/101566951#msg1771 for example.
This reads like it is trying to further restrict the AGPL into a Source-Available license.  My vote is to reject this.
Thanks all. Given the comments in this thread from participants, I'm going to mark this one as not accepted and close the issue.
